behavior: Read chat messages from the active runtime snapshot
trigger: The runtime snapshot contains messages different from the legacy chat context, or the snapshot is absent.
expected: Show snapshot messages when present and fall back to legacy messages before a snapshot exists.
violation_example: The chat displays stale context messages after the active runtime changes.

behavior: Expose runtime initialization and history loading in the chat
trigger: Runtime readiness is initializing or history.loading is true, then both become ready.
expected: The chat reports loading until initialization and history loading both finish.
violation_example: The history spinner disappears while runtime history is still loading.

behavior: Keep rendered message identity separate across tabs
trigger: Two chat tabs contain messages with the same message ID.
expected: The rendering key includes the active tab or session so switching tabs does not reuse the old message element.
violation_example: A message from the previous tab remains attached to a same-ID message in the new tab.

behavior: Use runtime status and errors for chat messages
trigger: Runtime status or error disagrees with legacy context state.
expected: Message rendering and retry/error controls follow the runtime status and error, with legacy fallback.
violation_example: The UI shows the previous context error or transmission state for the active runtime.

behavior: Route action-stream requests through the action endpoint
trigger: Mind-map, slide or image-filter actions use action-stream endpoint definitions.
expected: The client sends those requests to Endpoint.Action with their action ID.
violation_example: An action-stream request silently takes the deprecated workflow endpoint.

behavior: Stop a BYOK request when local lease creation fails
trigger: A workspace has local BYOK providers and its lease mutation fails.
expected: The request surfaces an error and never starts a remote text stream without the lease.
violation_example: The request proceeds without the intended local-provider lease.

behavior: Retry an action in its previous session
trigger: An action is retried after its first request created a session.
expected: Retry reuses the last action session and does not create a new message.
violation_example: Retry starts a new session or message, losing action continuity.

behavior: Attribute an action result to its initiating host
trigger: Two hosts have interleaved actions and the first host reports a result.
expected: The result event is attributed to that host action.
violation_example: The result is attributed to the most recent action on another host.

behavior: Load chat sessions and recent history with messages
trigger: The chat opens a session or lists recent sessions to derive titles.
expected: History queries request message bodies and retain them in the returned session.
violation_example: The list or opened session has IDs but no messages for title and content display.

behavior: Reuse the first matching element and remove duplicates
trigger: The container has two DOM elements matching the selector.
expected: Reuse the first object, remove the second, call configure, and create no new element.
violation_example: Append a duplicate or reuse the wrong object.

behavior: Update the configuration of an existing element on rerender
trigger: The configure input of the same hook instance changes from first to next.
expected: Keep a single element and update its value to next.
violation_example: Never update the initial configuration.

behavior: Create and configure no element while disabled
trigger: enabled=false and a container exists.
expected: Do not create, configure, or emit ready; create and append only after enabling.
violation_example: Create or configure DOM elements while disabled.

behavior: Notify readiness only once per element
trigger: The same element undergoes an effect rerun or a configuration update.
expected: Call onElementReady only for the first readiness notification.
violation_example: Repeat the readiness notification on every configure call.

behavior: Insert Markdown without leaving an extra document in the target workspace
trigger: The target workspace contains page0 and Markdown is inserted into a note on that page.
expected: The workspace still contains only page0 after the operation.
violation_example: Conversion through toDoc leaves a temporary document.

behavior: Show only enabled and selected workspace calendars
trigger: A workspace has enabled and disabled subscriptions and the view selects a subset.
expected: Only enabled IDs selected by the view contribute external entries.
violation_example: A disabled or unselected calendar leaks into the view.

behavior: Map external event times and metadata into calendar entries
trigger: An external event has UTC start/end, title and calendar metadata.
expected: The entry has the corresponding time range, identity, title and metadata.
violation_example: An event appears on the wrong day or loses its identity or title.

behavior: Choose a visible color and honor workspace override
trigger: A subscription has a muted account color and optionally a workspace color override.
expected: Muted colors get a stable visible replacement; an eligible workspace override takes priority.
violation_example: The event stays unreadable or ignores the workspace override.

behavior: Load external events only when source data is available
trigger: The workspace has no server, empty calendar caches, or a calendar request fails.
expected: No-server and failed requests return empty entries; empty caches load before fetching events.
violation_example: A missing server still triggers a request, or cold caches hide available events.

behavior: Open integration settings from the calendar connection entry
trigger: The user activates the external calendar connection entry.
expected: The workspace integration settings callback is invoked.
violation_example: The connect entry does nothing.

behavior: Expand a month to full weeks using the chosen first weekday
trigger: A month starts and ends midweek and weekStartsOn is Monday.
expected: The visible range includes surrounding days through complete weeks, with accurate month bounds.
violation_example: The first or final partial week is truncated or starts on Sunday.

behavior: Split spanning events across week boundaries without overlap
trigger: Two date-range entries overlap and one crosses a week boundary.
expected: Segments preserve each covered day and occupy distinct slots when overlapping.
violation_example: An event disappears after the first week or overlapping events share a slot.

behavior: Exclude the midnight end date of an all-day external event
trigger: An all-day external event runs from May 10 through an exclusive May 12 midnight end.
expected: The calendar covers May 10 and 11 only.
violation_example: The event also occupies May 12.

behavior: Move and resize calendar rows without corrupting date range
trigger: A dated row is moved to another day or a range edge is resized.
expected: The row start and end cells reflect the moved duration or adjusted edge.
violation_example: The row moves but its end remains on the old day, or range edges cross incorrectly.

behavior: Keep the latest external calendar response
trigger: Two calendar-range loads overlap and the older one completes last.
expected: The view retains the latest request result.
violation_example: An old month response replaces the active month entries.

behavior: Keep view options open while navigating nested pages
trigger: The user enters a nested view-options page and uses Back.
expected: The menu returns to the prior page without closing, then closes only on explicit dismissal.
violation_example: Back unexpectedly closes the menu and loses navigation context.

behavior: Initialize a ready draft tab when no historical session exists
trigger: The document scope has no pinned, pending, or document session.
expected: Readiness is ready, activeSessionId is empty, tabs contains only draft, and messages is empty.
violation_example: Initialization fails, activates the wrong session, or omits the draft tab.

behavior: Load full messages and activate an existing historical session
trigger: The document scope finds the latest session and getSession returns its full object with messages.
expected: The runtime calls getSession, loads messages from the full object, and reaches ready.
violation_example: Show only the list summary, lose messages, or remain in draft.

behavior: Resolve eligible host default conferencing preferences
trigger: A host has a dynamic app or static link; organizer-default is configured on a team/managed event, or these eligibility conditions are absent.
expected: Use the dynamic location type or static URL only when both the location setting and event eligibility permit it; otherwise use event locations.
violation_example: A normal personal event or an event without organizer-default unexpectedly adopts the host default.

behavior: Treat missing or unresolvable host preferences as unavailable
trigger: Host metadata has no app slug, or the referenced app has no usable location.
expected: Resolve no host default so the caller can use a configured fallback.
violation_example: An unknown app slug is returned as a usable conferencing location.

behavior: Fall back to the first configured real location, then Cal Video
trigger: No host default can be used; configured locations contain multiple real choices or only organizer-default.
expected: Pick the first real location with its credential; if none exists, use the real Cal Video type integrations:daily.
violation_example: Pick a later location or return a literal that does not identify Cal Video.

behavior: Resolve configured location value and optional credential
trigger: Location details are requested for an integration or static/in-person value, with or without a matching credential.
expected: Resolve the configured value and matching credential; absent credentials become null.
violation_example: Drop a configured credential or fail to resolve an in-person address.

behavior: Carry the new organizer location and credential into rescheduling
trigger: Manual reassignment changes the organizer with a different default app, static link, or configured credential.
expected: The actual reassignment passes the new location and relevant credential to EventManager and persists the location.
violation_example: The resolver is correct but reassignment still reschedules using the old location or drops the credential.

behavior: Retain conference credential when the organizer remains fixed
trigger: A fixed organizer remains while a round-robin attendee is reassigned; the existing location has a credential.
expected: Pass that credential into EventManager without requiring an organizer change.
violation_example: The unchanged-organizer branch leaves conferenceCredentialId undefined.

behavior: Report Cal Video failure during reassignment
trigger: Rescheduling returns a failed daily_video result.
expected: Reject with the explicit message that conferencing failed although the meeting was rescheduled.
violation_example: Silently continue after daily_video success=false.

behavior: Apply the current user booking filter
trigger: User selects My Bookings.
expected: Apply the current user ID filter to the bookings table.
violation_example: Apply another user ID or select the label without applying the filter.

behavior: Apply saved segment table state
trigger: A segment specifies filters, sort, column visibility/width, page size and search.
expected: Apply its specified state and reset page index.
violation_example: Selected segment label updates but sort or pagination remains from the previous state.

behavior: Persist selecting and clearing a system segment
trigger: User selects or deselects a system segment and revisits the table.
expected: Restore selected segment identity, or remain unselected after explicit clearing.
violation_example: Cleared selection reappears on revisit.

behavior: Clear system selection after manual filter or page-size changes
trigger: A selected system segment is followed by adding/changing/removing a filter or changing page size.
expected: Clear selected system identity and retain the manual change.
violation_example: System segment stays selected despite manual changes.

behavior: Offer duplication but no rename/delete for built-in segments
trigger: User opens a system segment submenu.
expected: Duplicate is available; Rename and Delete are absent.
violation_example: Built-in segment offers destructive mutation controls.

behavior: Respect ownership rules for personal and team segment menus
trigger: Personal segment or team segment is opened by an admin/owner versus ordinary member.
expected: Personal controls are available; team rename/delete are restricted to admin/owner.
violation_example: A member can rename a shared team segment through its submenu.

behavior: Save changes with correct create/update mode and select a newly created segment
trigger: Current selection is system or user segment and current table state has changed.
expected: Create for system/no selection, allow update for user segment, select returned created segment; enable saving when state differs.
violation_example: System segment is submitted as an update or new segment remains unselected.

behavior: Discard inaccessible segment identity while preserving current filters
trigger: A supplied segment ID cannot be found among accessible segments.
expected: Clear segment identity/preference without overwriting the other current query state.
violation_example: Inaccessible ID clears independently specified filters too.

behavior: Combine built-in and saved segments with distinct IDs and refreshed date ranges
trigger: System and user segments coexist, including relative date filters.
expected: Keep identities distinct, refresh relative ranges and display system/personal/team groups.
violation_example: ID collision selects the wrong type or date filter remains stale.

behavior: Return categories in ascending position order
trigger: The allIds order differs from the categories' numeric position order.
expected: Return category objects in ascending numeric position order.
violation_example: Continue returning categories in allIds order.

behavior: Place categories with null or undefined positions last
trigger: Numeric positions are mixed with null or undefined positions.
expected: Place every category without a position after categories with numeric positions.
violation_example: Treat null as zero and place it first.

behavior: Ignore category IDs missing from byId
trigger: allIds contains an ID absent from byId.
expected: Return no undefined entries and sort without throwing.
violation_example: Retain undefined entries or fail while reading their positions.

behavior: Send reordered category positions as positions_hash
trigger: The category reorder API receives reorderedGroup.
expected: The POST categories/reorder body contains positions_hash equal to reorderedGroup.
violation_example: Omit positions_hash or send the old mapping.

behavior: Update article positions locally and restore them when reordering fails
trigger: The article reorder action receives valid reorderedGroup and the API succeeds or fails.
expected: Commit the new positions on success; on failure commit the old positions and rethrow the original error.
violation_example: Retain new positions after API failure or swallow the error.

behavior: Update category positions locally and restore them when reordering fails
trigger: The category reorder action receives valid reorderedGroup and the API succeeds or fails.
expected: Commit the new positions on success; on failure commit the old positions and rethrow the original error.
violation_example: Retain new positions after API failure or swallow the error.

behavior: Update entity positions and reorder allIds in the position mutation
trigger: An article or category SET_*_POSITIONS mutation receives positions for multiple entities.
expected: Update the corresponding entities and order allIds by ascending position.
violation_example: Update positions without sorting or return the wrong entity order.

behavior: Parse valid natural-language dates and reject invalid dates
trigger: parseDateFromText receives a relative duration, relative date, or invalid text.
expected: Return a future Date and unix value for valid input; return null for invalid or past dates.
violation_example: Accept an invalid date or return null for a valid future date.

behavior: Generate a bounded set of valid date suggestions
trigger: generateDateSuggestions receives a complete date or partial date text.
expected: Return at most five relevant future candidates and no irrelevant suggestions measured in seconds.
violation_example: Return invalid candidates, exceed the limit, or produce suggestions measured in seconds.

behavior: Convert snooze candidates into suggestions with timestamps and display fields
trigger: generateSnoozeSuggestions receives valid natural language.
expected: Include date, unixTime, query, label, formattedDate, and resolve; expand abbreviated units into readable labels.
violation_example: Omit timestamp or display fields, or leave abbreviated labels unexpanded.

behavior: Export parser and suggestion functions through the public snoozeDateParser entry
trigger: Both functions are imported from the snoozeDateParser directory entry.
expected: Make parseDateFromText and generateDateSuggestions callable through that entry.
violation_example: Omit either export or require importing an internal file.

behavior: Return articles in ascending position order
trigger: Article positions differ from the allIds order.
expected: Order the result by numeric position.
violation_example: Preserve the original allIds order.

behavior: Place articles without positions after positioned articles
trigger: Numeric, null, and undefined positions are mixed.
expected: Place both null and undefined positions after numeric entries.
violation_example: Treat null as zero and place it early.

behavior: Ignore deleted article IDs
trigger: allIds contains an ID absent from byId.
expected: Filter out that entry and sort the remaining objects.
violation_example: Return undefined or throw while reading its position.

behavior: Forward the caller's AbortSignal from ContactAPI.search to axios
trigger: ContactAPI.search receives options.signal.
expected: The second axios.get argument contains the same signal.
violation_example: Lose the signal at the transport boundary.

behavior: Block contact queries shorter than two characters by default
trigger: createContactSearcher receives an empty or single-character query.
expected: Return an empty array without calling ContactAPI.search; skipMinLength can bypass the single-character restriction.
violation_example: Send a single-character request by default or ignore the explicit bypass.

behavior: Cancel an earlier search and return null for cancellation errors
trigger: The same searcher starts two successive requests, or a request fails with AbortError or CanceledError.
expected: Abort the earlier signal, return null for cancellation errors, and rethrow ordinary errors.
violation_example: Keep the earlier request running or throw cancellation as an ordinary error.

behavior: Build macro dropdown options from verified agents while retaining Self
trigger: The verified getter returns a nonempty or empty list and assign_agent options are read.
expected: Put Self before the verified list when nonempty; return only Self when empty.
violation_example: Continue using getAgents and fail to obtain the verified list.

behavior: Do not insert a conversation with an existing ID
trigger: The list already contains id=1 and receives another object with id=1.
expected: Keep only the original conversation.
violation_example: Push a duplicate conversation with the same ID.

behavior: Read verified agents in the automation module
trigger: useAutomation initializes and the verified getter returns an agents fixture.
expected: computedAgents.value equals the agents supplied by the verified getter.
violation_example: Continue using getAgents and fail to obtain the verified list.

behavior: Validate document and template search query bounds
trigger: Query is blank/whitespace, over 1024 characters or valid text with surrounding spaces.
expected: Reject blank/overlong queries and trim valid queries before searching.
violation_example: Whitespace-only or oversized query is accepted.

behavior: Search allowed document fields within the user access scope
trigger: User searches by title, externalId or recipient email, across own and permitted team documents.
expected: Match these fields while excluding unrelated teams and deleted documents.
violation_example: Recipient-email search returns an inaccessible team document.

behavior: Honor document visibility at the user highest team role
trigger: Admin, manager or member searches documents with EVERYONE/MANAGER_AND_ABOVE/ADMIN visibility.
expected: Return only documents allowed to that role.
violation_example: Manager gets an ADMIN document instead of the allowed manager document.

behavior: Search permitted templates by title or recipient email
trigger: Own/team templates coexist with other-team and soft-deleted templates.
expected: Return matching nondeleted accessible templates.
violation_example: Deleted or other-team templates are returned, or recipient email never matches.

behavior: Honor per-role template visibility
trigger: Admin, manager and member search three template visibility levels.
expected: Return the exact permitted template subset.
violation_example: Manager gets an ADMIN template in place of a manager template.

behavior: Authenticate the template search endpoint
trigger: Unauthenticated client calls template.search.
expected: Reject the request.
violation_example: Return a search response without authentication.

behavior: Limit results after role filtering
trigger: More than the requested limit of candidate envelopes exist and some fail role visibility.
expected: Filter candidates and return no more than limit; do not truncate the initial candidate fetch at limit before applying visibility.
violation_example: Dropping post-filter slicing returns more than limit.

behavior: Display template search results in the command menu
trigger: Open command menu and search for an accessible template.
expected: The corresponding template option appears.
violation_example: API finds a template but command menu never renders it.

behavior: Search only while the menu is open with nonblank text
trigger: Menu is closed or query is cleared to whitespace after a prior search.
expected: Do not start search requests and do not display previous results for a blank query.
violation_example: Previous results remain visible after the query is cleared.

behavior: Show loading state separately for document and template groups
trigger: One search request is pending while the other has data.
expected: Render the loading indicator in the pending group and completed results in the other.
violation_example: One pending request hides or mislabels the other group results.

behavior: Navigate to workspace routes from environment and project controls
trigger: User opens project configuration or switches projects from the environment navigation.
expected: The destination uses /workspace/ settings routes and /workspaces/ project landing routes.
violation_example: Navigation still points to the removed /project/ or /projects/ URLs.

behavior: Enter workspace onboarding and present workspace identity
trigger: New user starts onboarding and creates a workspace.
expected: Onboarding uses /workspaces/new and workspace labels in creation settings.
violation_example: The onboarding flow waits at an old projects/new path or presents project creation labels.

behavior: Use workspace wording in settings, permissions and languages
trigger: Workspace settings or language management is rendered, or a workspace permission/action error occurs.
expected: Visible labels, confirmations and error messages use workspace terminology and the updated translation keys.
violation_example: One surface continues showing project wording or a missing translation key.

behavior: Report a workspace-specific duplicate-name error
trigger: Creating a workspace hits Prisma unique constraint P2002.
expected: Reject with InvalidInputError naming workspace.
violation_example: Still reports A project with this name already exists.

behavior: Use the correct field label and registration key
trigger: CommitMessageTemplateField is rendered.
expected: Show Commit message template and pass commit.singleResourceMessageTemplate to register.
violation_example: Register the input under the wrong key.

behavior: Preserve literal double-brace variables in placeholder text
trigger: The default placeholder and help text are rendered.
expected: Preserve action/title in the placeholder and double-brace action/resourceKind/resourceID/title in the help text.
violation_example: Let i18n consume the template variables before use.

behavior: Trim a valid commit template before writing it to spec
trigger: The form supplies a nonempty template with leading or trailing whitespace.
expected: spec.commit.singleResourceMessageTemplate equals the trimmed template.
violation_example: Preserve surrounding whitespace or omit the template.

behavior: Omit commit when its template is unset or blank
trigger: commit is unset or the template contains only spaces.
expected: spec.commit is absent.
violation_example: Emit a commit object with an empty template.

behavior: Route legacy alert preview to its named policy
trigger: Legacy label-based routing is active and the alert has a named-root policy label.
expected: The preview receives that policy name; the new routing-settings mode uses selectedPolicy.
violation_example: The preview always uses the root policy despite a named-root label.

behavior: Hide the routing infrastructure label from preview details
trigger: An alert instance contains NAMED_ROOT_LABEL_NAME and an ordinary label.
expected: Only ordinary labels appear as potential instance details.
violation_example: The internal routing label is shown to users.

behavior: Show explanatory tooltip only for disabled preview
trigger: The notification preview is enabled or disabled by its prerequisites.
expected: Wrap the button with a tooltip only when preview is disabled.
violation_example: An enabled preview still shows the disabled-state explanation.

behavior: Add stored dashboard panels when editing becomes active
trigger: A dashboard opens with pending panels under dashboardNewLayouts, while its edit pane is inactive or active.
expected: Inactive scenes wait for edit-pane activation; active scenes add panels immediately and consume stored data once.
violation_example: Panels are inserted before editing starts or are lost before activation.

behavior: Include all log frame fields in full JSON export
trigger: A log frame includes a linked field, entry field or DataPlane LogLines metadata.
expected: The full JSON fields record includes every available log.fields value.
violation_example: The exporter silently omits linked or DataPlane fields.

behavior: Preserve large numbers in exported log JSON
trigger: A log entry contains a JSON number beyond JavaScript safe integer precision.
expected: Export serializes the parsed lossless value without rounding.
violation_example: JSON.stringify rounds or changes the numeric token.

behavior: Fall back when log ID or nanosecond fields have empty row values
trigger: A log frame declares id and tsNs fields, but their value arrays have no value for a row.
expected: Use the row index for uid, omit rowId and derive timeEpochNs from the timestamp.
violation_example: The uid contains undefined or an empty nanosecond value replaces the derived timestamp.

behavior: Infer log level from text only when the flag is enabled
trigger: A line contains a recognizable level and the GrafanaLogLevelInference flag is on or off.
expected: Inference returns its level when enabled and unknown when disabled.
violation_example: The same level is inferred despite the feature flag being off.

behavior: Suggest an available plugin update on import failure
trigger: A plugin module load fails with hasUpdate true or false.
expected: Show the named update suggestion only when an update exists; otherwise retain the generic error.
violation_example: The importer always shows a generic message despite an available update.

behavior: Remove redundant scope_node when a scope has defaultPath
trigger: An applied scope has a nonempty defaultPath and the URL is updated.
expected: Write scopes but clear scope_node; retain the selected node only when no defaultPath supplies it.
violation_example: A stale scope_node remains in the URL and overrides the default path.

behavior: Wait for scope metadata before enabling URL sync
trigger: Scopes are enabled while the selected scope metadata has not loaded.
expected: Do not write a stale URL; synchronize after metadata arrives.
violation_example: setEnabled immediately writes an old scope_node before the metadata is known.

behavior: Hide Remove all in scopes-first mode
trigger: The scopes-first feature flag is enabled with applied scopes.
expected: The tooltip offers no Remove all action; normal enabled mode retains it.
violation_example: A user in scopes-first mode can remove every scope.

behavior: Expose CloudWatch log-group page token from the Link header
trigger: The log-groups response has a next Link header or no next link.
expected: Return the result array and extracted nextToken so callers can request another page.
violation_example: The first page is returned with no token and further groups are unreachable.

behavior: Append CloudWatch log groups from later pages
trigger: The first search page returns a nextToken and the user clicks Load more.
expected: Request the next page with the current search filters, append its groups, and hide Load more when no token remains.
violation_example: The control resets results or requests the first page again.

behavior: Report a failed CloudWatch next-page request
trigger: The first page succeeds but requesting the next page rejects.
expected: Keep the first-page groups and publish an error notification.
violation_example: The failure silently empties the current list.

behavior: Keep field and variable log-group options after response shape change
trigger: CloudWatch returns a results object instead of a bare group array.
expected: The log-group field and variable support still present the groups from response.results.
violation_example: A consumer maps the response object as an array and shows no groups.

behavior: Offer the logs table only when its feature flag is on
trigger: A log panel qualifies for a logs-table suggestion and logsTablePanelNG is on or off.
expected: Return the suggestion only when the flag is on.
violation_example: The suggestion remains visible when the flag is off.

behavior: Show and switch between recent and starred dashboards
trigger: Homepage loads with recent and starred dashboard data, and user selects either tab.
expected: Show the selected list on the homepage with distinct recent/starred counts.
violation_example: The homepage omits the tabs, shows the wrong list, or gives both tabs the same count.

behavior: Select the populated tab after initial loading
trigger: Initial recent list is empty while starred list is nonempty, or the reverse.
expected: After both loads finish, select the nonempty tab once without overriding later user selection.
violation_example: An empty tab remains selected, or a later refresh resets a user-selected tab.

behavior: Explain empty dashboard lists
trigger: Recent or starred list has no dashboards; recent-list user may or may not have dashboard-create permission.
expected: Show each list own empty state and a create/browse action appropriate to the recent-list permission.
violation_example: Empty tabs have no message or a noncreator receives a create action.

behavior: Report loading errors and retry each list
trigger: Recent or starred request is pending or fails.
expected: Show list-specific loading/error feedback and let Retry rerun the failed request.
violation_example: An error looks like an empty list or Retry does not rerun the request.

behavior: Clear recently viewed dashboard history
trigger: Recent list contains dashboard impressions and user clicks Clear history.
expected: Clear the organization-scoped stored impressions and reload the recent list.
violation_example: The displayed list disappears without clearing storage or the list never refreshes.

behavior: Refresh starred list after star change
trigger: A listed dashboard is unstarred from its list item.
expected: Refresh the starred query so the list reflects the change.
violation_example: The removed star remains in the displayed list.

behavior: Accept plugin homepage tabs
trigger: A plugin registers a content tab or a link tab through HomepageTabs.
expected: Show each unique content tab with content when selected and link tabs as links.
violation_example: Plugin tab is missing, duplicated, or displays no content.

behavior: Render repository commit templates
trigger: Repository has a nonempty single-resource template with supported and unknown placeholders.
expected: Replace all occurrences of action, resourceKind, resourceID and title; leave unknown placeholders intact.
violation_example: A supported placeholder remains literal or an unknown placeholder is deleted.

behavior: Choose comment, template or built-in commit message
trigger: A user comment is nonblank, whitespace-only or absent; template may also be absent.
expected: Use trimmed nonblank comment first, otherwise template, otherwise the appropriate dashboard/folder default.
violation_example: Whitespace-only comment creates a blank commit or bypasses a configured template.

behavior: Send resolved messages from dashboard forms
trigger: User creates/updates, moves or deletes a provisioned dashboard with a repository template.
expected: The corresponding request carries the rendered template using the actual dashboard action and details.
violation_example: Helper works alone but one dashboard form still sends a hardcoded message.

behavior: Send resolved messages from folder forms
trigger: User creates, renames or deletes a provisioned folder with a repository template.
expected: Each request carries a message derived from the corresponding action and folder details.
violation_example: The helper works but a folder form still sends a hardcoded message.

behavior: Delete only a token owned by the specified user
trigger: deletePAT(tokenId,userUid) is called.
expected: The deleteMany condition includes both the token ID and caller UID.
violation_example: Omit userUid from the database deletion condition.

behavior: Distinguish successful deletion from not-found using the deleted count
trigger: deleteMany returns count=0 or count=1.
expected: Return NOT_FOUND Left for zero and true Right for one.
violation_example: Report successful deletion when count=0.

behavior: Look up personal collections within the requesting user
trigger: Two users have collections; caller requests a collection ID owned by one or the other.
expected: Query by both collection ID and caller UID and return not-found for a foreign collection.
violation_example: A foreign collection is returned from an ID-only query.

behavior: Reject a foreign parent when creating a personal collection
trigger: User creates a child collection under a parent owned by another user.
expected: Parent lookup is scoped to that user and creation fails without attaching under the foreign parent.
violation_example: The child is created under an ID-only foreign parent.

behavior: Reject foreign personal collection mutations
trigger: User deletes, moves or reorders a personal collection, or supplies a foreign destination.
expected: Look up each source/destination in the caller scope and reject foreign IDs before mutation.
violation_example: A foreign collection is deleted, moved or used as a reorder destination.

behavior: Restrict personal collection export and duplication to the owner
trigger: User exports a collection subtree or duplicates it from a supplied collection ID.
expected: Every root and recursive child lookup remains scoped to that user.
violation_example: An ID-only lookup leaks a foreign subtree during export or duplication.

behavior: Reject a request created inside a foreign collection
trigger: User creates a request using a collection ID owned by another user.
expected: Resolve the collection under the authenticated UID and return not-found before creating a request.
violation_example: A request is inserted into a foreign collection.

behavior: Scope both collections during request moves
trigger: An authenticated user moves a request between source and destination collections, one of which belongs to another user.
expected: Validate both collections under the authenticated UID and reject an inaccessible collection.
violation_example: A request is moved into a foreign collection because one lookup used an ID alone.

behavior: Keep one slug across versions of a collection
trigger: A collection is published for the first time and subsequently with another version.
expected: Generate a slug for the first publication and reuse that slug for the same collection and workspace.
violation_example: Every version gets an unrelated slug, so one public slug cannot identify its versions.

behavior: Bound retries for a publication version conflict
trigger: Creation collides on the slug-version uniqueness constraint or fails for an unrelated reason.
expected: Retry a uniqueness conflict at most twice; return a creation error after three attempts and do not retry unrelated failures.
violation_example: A conflict fails immediately or an unrelated database error is retried indefinitely.

behavior: List versions by slug with current versions first
trigger: A slug has multiple versions with different autoSync and creation times, or has no records.
expected: Return only that slug, ordered by autoSync then newest creation time, and report not-found when empty.
violation_example: Versions from another slug leak in, a stale version is selected first, or an empty slug succeeds.

behavior: Resolve public documents by slug and selected version
trigger: An unauthenticated request supplies a slug and an explicit version, omits the version, or uses an unknown slug/version.
expected: Resolve the explicit slug-version pair or the first ordered version, and return not-found when no matching document exists.
violation_example: A request for an older version returns a different version or an unknown pair resolves by document ID.

behavior: Expose all versions in the public document response
trigger: A public document has more than one version.
expected: The response includes the available version objects with their slug, version, title and URL.
violation_example: The public document resolves but its versions list is absent or contains only the requested version.

behavior: Build public URLs from slug and version
trigger: A published document is returned with an internal ID different from its slug.
expected: Its public URL uses the slug and version, not the internal record ID.
violation_example: The returned URL still contains the internal ID.

behavior: Export the current full collection for auto-sync documents
trigger: A published user or team document has autoSync enabled and its collection has nested children.
expected: Public retrieval exports the current full collection without caller-controlled tree filtering.
violation_example: The response uses a stale tree or truncates children because of a shallow-export option.

behavior: Freeze a collection snapshot when auto-sync is off
trigger: A document is created without autoSync, then its source collection changes before public retrieval.
expected: Creation stores the exported tree and public retrieval uses the stored tree; autoSync creation stores no snapshot.
violation_example: Public retrieval silently uses the current collection despite autoSync being off.

behavior: Update the snapshot when auto-sync changes
trigger: An existing document switches from autoSync on to off, or from off to on.
expected: Capture the current tree when turning sync off and clear the stored tree when turning it on.
violation_example: A newly unsynced document has no frozen tree, or a synced document retains stale data.

behavior: Attach only an environment from the publication workspace
trigger: A user or team creates a publication with an environment ID from that workspace or a foreign/unknown ID.
expected: Look up the environment under the workspace owner, persist its name and variables, and reject an inaccessible ID.
violation_example: A publication embeds variables from a foreign user or team environment.

behavior: Replace, remove or preserve a publication environment
trigger: An editor supplies a new accessible environment, null, or omits the environment field during update.
expected: Store the new environment, clear all three fields on null, or leave them unchanged when omitted; reject an unknown ID.
violation_example: A removed environment still exposes old variables or a title-only update clears it.

behavior: Refresh a live publication environment but retain snapshot values
trigger: A public document with autoSync on has a linked environment whose variables have changed, or autoSync is off.
expected: Re-fetch the linked environment for live docs; use stored values for snapshots and reject a missing linked environment.
violation_example: Live docs expose stale variables, or a frozen version silently changes after its environment is edited.

behavior: Serialize publication environment fields in API responses
trigger: A document has environment variables or has no associated environment.
expected: Return the environment name and JSON-stringified variables, or null fields when absent.
violation_example: Variables are omitted or returned as an unserialized object.

behavior: Wait for stale publication deletion during list cleanup
trigger: Listing published documents finds records whose collections no longer exist.
expected: The cleanup deletion completes before the list operation finishes.
violation_example: The list returns while the stale-record delete remains unresolved.

behavior: Authorize personal environment updates by owner
trigger: User A updates an environment ID belonging to user B.
expected: The update query includes A UID and cannot modify B environment.
violation_example: An ID-only update changes B environment.

behavior: Authorize personal environment deletion by owner
trigger: User A deletes an environment ID belonging to user B.
expected: The delete query includes A UID and cannot remove B environment.
violation_example: An ID-only delete removes B environment.

behavior: Authorize clearing personal environment variables by owner
trigger: User A clears variables in an environment ID belonging to user B.
expected: The clear operation includes A UID in its update query and cannot erase B variables.
violation_example: An ID-only clear erases another user environment.

behavior: Use database ID and title in exportUserCollectionToJSONObject
trigger: Request payload id/name conflicts with database row id/title.
expected: The exported request.id/name in exportUserCollectionToJSONObject comes from the database row.
violation_example: Let the payload overwrite database metadata.

behavior: Use database ID and title in exportUserCollectionsToJSON
trigger: Request payload id/name conflicts with database row id/title.
expected: The exported request.id/name in exportUserCollectionsToJSON comes from the database row.
violation_example: Let the payload overwrite database metadata.

behavior: Restrict plugin behavior to component references
trigger: A typed PayloadComponent string, an object path/exportName, and an unrelated string occur in one TS project.
expected: Recognize the component forms, including their sibling values, without treating unrelated strings as component references.
violation_example: Ordinary strings receive component diagnostics or component suggestions, or object exportName is ignored.

behavior: Report unresolved component paths
trigger: A PayloadComponent refers to a nonexistent module through a slash path or a tsconfig alias; valid paths also occur.
expected: Emit diagnostic 71001 for the missing module while leaving the valid paths free of plugin path errors.
violation_example: The bad path is silently accepted, or a valid path receives the same error.

behavior: Check named and default component exports
trigger: A resolvable module is referenced with an existing or missing named/default export, including object exportName and aliases.
expected: Emit 71002 for absent exports, accept present exports and honor the object exportName override.
violation_example: A nonexistent export is accepted or a valid sibling exportName still triggers a missing-default error.

behavior: Provide a useful missing-export message
trigger: A component names a missing export in a module that has other exports.
expected: The diagnostic names the missing export and offers a spelling suggestion when available, otherwise lists available exports.
violation_example: The diagnostic gives no candidate export or names the wrong missing member.

behavior: Complete component module paths
trigger: The cursor is inside a component path at a base-directory slash or an @/ alias directory.
expected: Offer matching component files and directories from the resolved location.
violation_example: No suggestions appear, or suggestions come from the wrong directory.

behavior: Complete component exports
trigger: The cursor is after # or inside object exportName for a resolvable component module, including an @/ alias.
expected: Offer the module actual named/default exports as completion entries.
violation_example: Offer path names or no exports at an export position.

behavior: Navigate to component file and export
trigger: Go-to-definition is requested on a component reference with named/default export, object form or @/ alias.
expected: Navigate to the resolved file and named export where available.
violation_example: Navigation goes to another file or only to the file when the named export is present.

behavior: Resolve slash paths from Payload config directory
trigger: A config file is found above the edited TS file, or plugin baseDir is explicitly configured.
expected: Resolve slash-prefixed component paths from the detected or configured base directory.
violation_example: Resolution incorrectly starts from the edited file directory or ignores configured baseDir.

behavior: Parse absolute and local start times
trigger: parseStartTime receives an explicit UTC/offset timestamp, or an offset-free local timestamp with or without a time zone.
expected: Explicit offsets remain authoritative; local timestamps use the supplied zone or UTC, and the requested duration is retained.
violation_example: A +05:30 timestamp is interpreted in the supplied zone, or an offset-free New York time is treated as UTC.

behavior: Deduplicate slots by instant and duration
trigger: The input has two equal (startTime, duration) pairs and a pair with the same instant but different duration.
expected: Equal pairs collapse to one; differing durations remain distinct.
violation_example: Deduplication compares only startTime and drops a distinct duration.

behavior: Select allowed weekdays across the inclusive date range
trigger: A date range spans multiple weekdays and daysOfWeek selects a subset.
expected: Generate slots for each matching date including range endpoints, and none for nonmatching days.
violation_example: Only the first day is considered, or slots are emitted on a disallowed weekday.

behavior: Space generated slots and keep the full duration within a window
trigger: A selected day has a bounded from/to window, a duration, and an optional custom interval.
expected: Slots start at the requested interval while start plus duration fits in the window; duration longer than the window yields none.
violation_example: A slot extends beyond toTime, or a custom interval is ignored.

behavior: Convert local slot windows to the requested time zone
trigger: The same local 09:00 window is generated in New York and with no time zone.
expected: Start instants reflect New York offset when specified and UTC otherwise.
violation_example: The New York slot starts at 09:00Z instead of 14:00Z.

behavior: Reject a non-increasing daily time window
trigger: On a selected day, toTime is before or equal to fromTime.
expected: No slots are generated for that day.
violation_example: A reversed or zero-length window emits a slot.

behavior: Construct poll administration and invitation URLs from the ID
trigger: Poll creation succeeds in date or time-slot mode and returns a poll ID.
expected: adminUrl is absoluteUrl(/poll/id) and inviteUrl is shortUrl(/invite/id).
violation_example: Depend on old URL fields no longer returned by the API core.

behavior: Classify the workspace selected by API Client
trigger: The view is SINGLE and API Client selects a LOCAL_STORAGE workspace.
expected: useMigrationSegment returns local-storage without substituting the global PERSONAL placeholder.
violation_example: Read the global default workspace and return auto-cloud.

behavior: Return unknown before workspaces have loaded
trigger: The view is SINGLE and the selected workspace list is empty.
expected: Return unknown.
violation_example: Treat an empty list as PERSONAL and return auto-cloud.

behavior: Drop an extension whose relative URL cannot be resolved
trigger: An extension URL is relative and its parent app has no appUrl; an absolute URL may still be present.
expected: The unresolved relative extension is omitted, while an absolute URL remains usable.
violation_example: The relative extension appears with a broken destination, or the absolute extension is discarded too.

behavior: Hide MANAGE_APPS from custom-extension permission choices
trigger: The shop permission list contains MANAGE_APPS alongside a permissible code.
expected: The custom-extension selector omits MANAGE_APPS and retains the permissible option.
violation_example: A user can select MANAGE_APPS for a custom extension, or permissible options disappear.

behavior: Explain missing configuration screen on third-party app details
trigger: A third-party app has no appUrl; compare an app with appUrl and a local app.
expected: A no-configuration notice appears only for the third-party app without appUrl.
violation_example: The notice is absent for that app, or appears for a local/configured app.

behavior: Send installed apps without appUrl to their manage screen
trigger: An active installed third-party app has no appUrl, compared with an active app that has one.
expected: The no-URL app link targets the manage/edit route; the configured app link targets its view route.
violation_example: An active app with no appUrl opens an unusable iframe view.

behavior: Redirect direct iframe navigation when an app has no appUrl
trigger: The user navigates directly to a manifest app iframe route whose app has no appUrl.
expected: The view redirects to the app manage screen; an app with appUrl still renders its page.
violation_example: The no-URL route renders a blank page or tries to load an empty iframe URL.

behavior: Boolean attributes return fixed Yes/No choices without querying GraphQL choices
trigger: A conditional filter asks for choices for an attribute whose input type is BOOLEAN.
expected: The handler returns the two boolean options and makes no choices query.
violation_example: If the handler queried the attribute choices endpoint or returned server choices, the boolean filter contract would be violated.

behavior: The selected attribute type is passed into the choices handler so the boolean branch is reachable
trigger: The selected filter value contains an attribute type and the query-variable builder creates an AttributeChoicesHandler.
expected: The handler receives the selected type; a BOOLEAN selection therefore uses the static branch while non-boolean selections retain query behavior.
violation_example: Dropping the type at handler construction makes the new boolean branch unreachable even if the handler itself is correct.

behavior: Show purchasability and shipping issues under separate headings
trigger: A channel has issues from both categories.
expected: Each issue appears under its own correctly named category section, with no old generic heading.
violation_example: Shipping issues appear under Purchasability or all issues remain in one generic Delivery configuration block.

behavior: Do not render empty category or delivery sections
trigger: Issues include only one recognized category, no issues, or solely an unrecognized future category.
expected: Only populated recognized sections appear; no empty bordered delivery section appears.
violation_example: An empty category heading or empty delivery box remains visible.

behavior: Use shop stock mode in availability diagnostics
trigger: The query returns an explicit true/false stock mode, or shop data is absent.
expected: Expose that mode and pass it into availability checks, with legacy=true fallback when absent.
violation_example: Direct mode is replaced by legacy mode or never reaches availability checks.

behavior: Keep stock mode available in nonready diagnostics
trigger: Diagnostics are disabled, product is absent, or query is loading.
expected: Still return the known shop mode or the legacy fallback.
violation_example: Early return omits the flag or overwrites a known direct mode.

behavior: Display the active stock-availability mode and its meaning
trigger: AvailabilityCard has channel results in legacy or direct mode.
expected: Show the corresponding mode label and tooltip explanation; do not show them while loading.
violation_example: Direct mode displays the legacy label or explanation.

behavior: Exclude info advisories from channel header issue presentation
trigger: Channel has info-only, warning-only, or mixed warning/error/info issues.
expected: Info-only leaves normal availability status; count only warnings/errors and prioritize error severity in badge/status.
violation_example: Info promotes a healthy channel to Issues or inflates the warning/error count.

behavior: Give each issue severity its own labeled visual
trigger: An error, warning or info callout/badge is shown.
expected: Render the matching visual and accessible severity label, including Information for info advisories.
violation_example: Info is rendered as a warning or icons lack accessible labels.

behavior: Do not generate a dashboard menu route for an absolute URL
trigger: extension.url is an absolute HTTPS URL.
expected: menu item.url is undefined and the resolver is not called.
violation_example: Call the resolver and generate an incorrect internal route.

behavior: Do not call the route resolver when appUrl is missing
trigger: The extension URL is relative and app.appUrl is null.
expected: menu item.url is undefined and the resolver is not called.
violation_example: Call the resolver and generate an incorrect internal route.

behavior: Include unresolved info advisories in the healthy summary
trigger: With full permissions, there are zero, one or multiple info advisories and no errors/warnings; warnings instead own the banner when present.
expected: Render no advisory suffix for zero, a singular count for one and the actual plural count for more; suppress this success banner when warnings exist.
violation_example: Show an unqualified healthy message despite an advisory, or show a literal count placeholder.

behavior: Distinguish stock availability from shipping feasibility
trigger: The API reports available stock, while shipping-zone count is zero, positive or unknown; the product may require shipping or be digital.
expected: Downgrade only shippable zero-zone products, with distinct legacy/direct wording; retain purchasable for digital products and positive/unknown coverage.
violation_example: Show Purchasable for a shippable zero-zone product, or wrongly downgrade a digital product.

behavior: Explain verification outcome using status and stock mode
trigger: Verification succeeds as purchasable, not purchasable or not visible, or is still loading/failed.
expected: Show the relevant explanation and stock-mode distinction for successful results, without reassurance while loading or failed.
violation_example: A direct-mode result explains legacy shipping-zone stock or loading shows successful reassurance.

behavior: Pass diagnostic mode and shipping facts into the displayed channel verdict
trigger: An expanded channel card has a verification result plus diagnostics specifying direct mode, digital status or zero/unknown shipping coverage.
expected: Its nested badge uses those diagnostic values and translates unknown coverage to undefined.
violation_example: Badge unit tests work but AvailabilityCard omits isShippingRequired or stock mode, causing an incorrect displayed verdict.

behavior: Explain warehouse configuration consequences
trigger: A missing-warehouse or uncovered-warehouse diagnostic is displayed.
expected: Explain customer unavailability and fulfillment impact, and legacy-zone remediation for uncovered stock.
violation_example: Continue presenting generic fulfillment-only text without the changed customer-visibility consequence.

behavior: Name voucher and promotion sources in line discounts
trigger: A line has no discount, an unnamed voucher, a named promotion, or multiple discounts.
expected: The source text uses the correct type label, includes names and separates multiple entries.
violation_example: A promotion is named as a voucher or multiple sources merge without separation.

behavior: Group nonzero line discounts by type and total their amounts
trigger: Order lines contain repeated discount types, quantities and zero-discount lines.
expected: Count discounted lines per type and sum unit discount times quantity; omit zero entries.
violation_example: The total ignores quantity or includes zero-discount lines.

behavior: Sum API-provided undiscounted line totals
trigger: Order lines contain gross and net undiscounted totals.
expected: Sum the requested gross or net API total across lines.
violation_example: The subtotal recomputes from discounted unit prices or always chooses gross.

behavior: Show combined order and line discount in the collapsed summary
trigger: An order has an order-level and line-level discount.
expected: The collapsed discount row shows their combined amount.
violation_example: The collapsed row shows only the order discount.

behavior: Show order and line discount details on expansion
trigger: A summary has order and line discounts and the user opens the discount row.
expected: Separate Order and Lines groups show type, amount and line count as applicable.
violation_example: The expanded row omits the line group or mislabels the discount type.

behavior: Show manual discount mode and reason in the summary
trigger: An editable order has a fixed or percentage manual discount with a reason.
expected: The expanded row shows the correct value mode and exposes the reason.
violation_example: A fixed discount is displayed as a percentage or its reason disappears.

behavior: Open the associated voucher from the discount summary
trigger: A voucher discount has a voucher ID and the user selects its name.
expected: Navigate to that voucher detail.
violation_example: The voucher name is inert or opens an unrelated voucher.

behavior: Expose undiscounted subtotal when it differs from the displayed subtotal
trigger: Discounts make the order subtotal lower than the gross undiscounted subtotal.
expected: A tooltip shows the before-discounts amount, and is absent when amounts match.
violation_example: The before-discounts amount is unavailable or shown for unchanged orders.

behavior: Convert entered discount value when switching mode
trigger: A user switches an entered fixed discount to percentage or the reverse.
expected: Preserve equivalent discount value using the order maximum and round to two decimals.
violation_example: Switching mode keeps the same numeric value with a different unit.

behavior: Reject malformed and excessive discount values
trigger: A user enters malformed, zero or above-limit percentage/fixed values.
expected: The form shows the matching error and disables confirmation.
violation_example: The form submits 150% or a fixed amount above the order maximum.

behavior: Show product, variant, SKU and quantity in order-line metadata header
trigger: A line metadata dialog opens for a variant with a SKU and quantity.
expected: Its header shows the product and variant and identifies SKU and quantity.
violation_example: The dialog loses line identity while editing metadata.

behavior: Use the router prefix by default
trigger: route.config has no own prefix and the router supplies /plugin.
expected: Concatenate the router prefix and route path.
violation_example: Produce an incorrect route path.

behavior: Let a route's own prefix override the router, including an empty string
trigger: route.config.prefix is /custom or an empty string.
expected: Prefer the route prefix; an empty string disables the router prefix.
violation_example: Produce an incorrect route path.

behavior: Normalize slashes after joining the route
trigger: The prefix has a trailing slash, the path has leading or trailing slashes, or the route is root.
expected: Collapse repeated slashes and remove a trailing slash while preserving root /.
violation_example: Produce an incorrect route path.

behavior: Default relationOpenMode to modal
trigger: The schema does not configure relationOpenMode and createDefaultSettings is called.
expected: Return relationOpenMode: modal.
violation_example: Omit the field or return page.

behavior: Let an explicit relationOpenMode override the default
trigger: schema.config.settings.relationOpenMode is page.
expected: createDefaultSettings returns page.
violation_example: Discard relationOpenMode when filtering settings and incorrectly retain modal.

behavior: Normalize email casing
trigger: An email includes uppercase local and domain letters.
expected: Return the lowercase address.
violation_example: Domain or local case is retained.

behavior: Decode UTF-8 encoded display words
trigger: Text contains Base64 or quoted-printable words, underscores for spaces or multiple encoded words.
expected: Decode encoded text and preserve surrounding plain text.
violation_example: Q underscores stay literal or only the first encoded word is decoded.

behavior: Encode short non-ASCII names while retaining ASCII names
trigger: An ASCII or short non-ASCII display name is passed to either encoder.
expected: ASCII remains unchanged; the other name receives its UTF-8 Base64 or Q encoding.
violation_example: ASCII is encoded unnecessarily or non-ASCII is corrupted.

behavior: Split long encoded names without splitting a UTF-8 character
trigger: A non-ASCII name exceeds one encoded-word chunk.
expected: Each word fits the declared length limit and decoding the words reconstructs the original name.
violation_example: The result is one overlong word or split bytes corrupt a character.

behavior: Extract nested comments while preserving quoted parentheses
trigger: Address text contains nested comments and quoted literal parentheses.
expected: Remove comments into an ordered list; preserve quoted content.
violation_example: Nested comments are cut short or quoted parentheses are stripped.

behavior: Unquote and unescape quoted display names
trigger: Display name is quoted with an escaped quote, or unquoted.
expected: Remove outer quoting and escape markers; retain an unquoted name.
violation_example: Escaped quote loses its character or outer quotes remain.

behavior: Extract normalized email and resolved display name while preserving input
trigger: Bare, angle-bracket, quoted, encoded or comment-based address; name and comment may coexist.
expected: Resolve explicit name ahead of comment fallback, normalize email and retain original text; nullish input yields empty fields.
violation_example: Comment replaces an explicit name, or original text is normalized destructively.

behavior: Format optional display names and respect encoding opt-out
trigger: Name is absent, ordinary, contains comma, or is non-ASCII with encoding enabled/disabled.
expected: Normalize email, quote comma names, encode non-ASCII by default and honor encodeNonAscii=false.
violation_example: Encoding cannot be disabled or the name/email presentation is wrong.

behavior: Validate address shape and declared length bounds
trigger: Valid or malformed address, dot-boundary local part, overlong local part/domain.
expected: Accept valid addresses and reject violations of the declared shape and length guards.
violation_example: A 65-character local part is accepted or a trailing-dot local part passes.

behavior: Split address lists without splitting quoted or nested comma content
trigger: Comma-separated addresses include quoted commas, comments with commas or escaped quote boundaries.
expected: Split only top-level separators and parse each address.
violation_example: A comma in a comment creates a spurious recipient.

behavior: Preserve explicit empty values while defaulting absent message values
trigger: Message text, html, from or replyTo is omitted or explicitly empty.
expected: Absent values use configured defaults or the other body format; explicit empty strings are retained.
violation_example: Explicit empty text is replaced by html or empty replyTo by its configured default.

behavior: Forward supported message content and metadata to the transport
trigger: send receives sender, alternative formats, headers, threading, encoding, calendar/list/envelope, security flags or raw MIME.
expected: The supplied supported values reach sendMail unchanged, including xMailer=false.
violation_example: An accepted option is silently dropped before transport.

behavior: Forward DSN and per-message OAuth credentials
trigger: send receives DSN plus user, refreshToken, accessToken and expiry.
expected: sendMail receives those values on the message.
violation_example: refreshToken or DSN is omitted.

behavior: Forward transport verification success and failure
trigger: Transport verify resolves or rejects.
expected: Provider verify preserves the result or rejection.
violation_example: Provider suppresses a connection error and returns true.

behavior: Return transport availability with a fallback for unsupported transports
trigger: Transport reports idle/busy or has no isIdle method.
expected: Preserve the returned boolean; return true if unsupported.
violation_example: Always returns true, or throws when the method is absent.

behavior: Close the owned transport
trigger: Client calls provider.close.
expected: Transport.close is called.
violation_example: The close method does nothing.

behavior: Expose nonsecret transport/auth information without credentials
trigger: Provider options include transport metadata and login/OAuth credentials.
expected: Report transport properties and auth type/user but omit passwords and tokens.
violation_example: Return the full auth object containing a password or token.

behavior: Report enabled transport features
trigger: Options enable some of OAuth2, DKIM, pooling, proxy, rate limiting or required TLS.
expected: Features reflect enabled options and omit absent options.
violation_example: Enabled proxy is unreported, or absent flags are always listed.

behavior: Fail a develop pull request without a milestone
trigger: base.ref=develop, labels are valid, and milestone is null or undefined.
expected: setFailed reports a milestone error.
violation_example: Incorrectly accept the pull request or reject a valid one.

behavior: Require no milestone for a pull request targeting another branch
trigger: base.ref=main, milestone=null, and the other constraints hold.
expected: Do not call setFailed.
violation_example: Incorrectly accept the pull request or reject a valid one.

behavior: Accept a develop pull request with a milestone
trigger: base.ref=develop, a milestone object exists, and labels are valid.
expected: Do not call setFailed.
violation_example: Incorrectly accept the pull request or reject a valid one.

behavior: Expose API grant controls in the E2E test environment even when flags are off
trigger: NEXT_PUBLIC_NODE_ENV is test while either or both feature flags are false.
expected: The grant-control hook returns true so the controls can be exercised by E2E tests.
violation_example: The hook still returns false because it requires live feature flags in test mode.

behavior: Keep the dual-flag gate outside test environments
trigger: NEXT_PUBLIC_NODE_ENV is not test.
expected: Grant controls are enabled only when both ConfigCat and PostHog flags are enabled.
violation_example: One enabled flag alone exposes the controls, or both enabled flags still hide them.

behavior: Give the privilege settings button an accessible name
trigger: The API privileges settings control is rendered.
expected: Assistive technology and role/name selectors identify the button as Configure API privileges.
violation_example: The icon-only button has no accessible name.

behavior: Fill missing components when parsing short versions
trigger: The input is 1 or 1.2.
expected: major=1 and missing minor or patch components become zero.
violation_example: Continue requiring three components and reject a short version.

behavior: Compare short versions with complete versions
trigger: A short version is compared with an equivalent, higher, or lower version.
expected: Fill missing components with zero and return the correct -1, 0, or 1.
violation_example: Continue requiring three components and reject a short version.

behavior: Accept short versions through the validation entry
trigger: isValidSemver receives 1 or 1.2.
expected: Return true.
violation_example: Continue requiring three components and reject a short version.

behavior: JSON configuration values are accepted only when they parse to an object; empty input becomes an empty object
trigger: The integration receives undefined/empty input, a valid object string, or a parsed primitive/array/null.
expected: Missing input returns {}, object JSON is returned, and non-object JSON raises a field-specific validation error.
violation_example: Passing [1], null, or 42 through as configuration would violate the object contract.

behavior: Convert non-Axios errors to human-readable messages
trigger: Non-Axios Error, primitive, object carrying a message (including nested Error), or unknown thrown value.
expected: Use Error.message, stringify primitives, recursively unwrap message properties, otherwise use the generic fallback.
violation_example: Return the generic fallback for an Error or nested message instead of its message.

behavior: Axios errors preserve response status/payload, no-response, and configuration distinctions
trigger: An AxiosError has response data, only a request, or neither.
expected: The formatter emits the corresponding status, no-response, or Axios-error prefix.
violation_example: Collapsing all Axios failures into one generic message loses actionable failure type.

behavior: validateConfiguration posts the validation probe and throws when the debug response contains validation messages
trigger: The debug endpoint returns zero or more validationMessages.
expected: Empty messages resolve; any messages are joined with field, description, and code details and cause rejection.
violation_example: A suite that tests only parsing helpers does not check whether invalid GA configuration is rejected.

behavior: trackEvent posts a collect payload with client/user ids and engagement time plus caller parameters
trigger: A caller invokes trackEvent with a user id, event name, and optional params.
expected: The collect request contains the ids, event name, engagement_time_msec=1, and supplied params.
violation_example: Testing only parsing cannot detect missing ids, event name, or engagement parameter.

behavior: updateUserProfile converts primitive values directly and serializes non-primitive values into user_properties before posting
trigger: A profile contains string, number, boolean, null, or object/array property values.
expected: Each property is wrapped as {value}; complex values are JSON-stringified and an update_user_profile event is sent.
violation_example: Passing an object directly would violate the GA user property value type.

behavior: Keep the current shipping address visible during editing
trigger: The order has a shipping address and the user clicks its Edit button.
expected: The existing shipping address remains visible while the selector is available.
violation_example: Clicking Edit replaces the address with a No shipping address placeholder.

behavior: Keep the current billing address visible during editing
trigger: The order has a billing address and the user clicks its Edit button.
expected: The existing billing address remains visible while the selector is available.
violation_example: Clicking billing Edit replaces the address with a No billing address placeholder.

behavior: Open the address selector immediately on Edit
trigger: The user clicks the Edit button beside an order address.
expected: The selector popover is open without a second click.
violation_example: The selector trigger appears but its popover stays closed.

behavior: Restore address editing state when the selector closes
trigger: The Edit selector is open and the user dismisses it without choosing an address.
expected: The popover closes and the page leaves editing mode, restoring the Edit control.
violation_example: The selector closes but the page stays in editing mode with no Edit control.

behavior: Finish plugin creation normally when the follow-up selection is cancelled
trigger: The basic plugin files exist and the follow-up selection returns a cancel symbol.
expected: Return the creation result without looking up or executing a command.
violation_example: Dereference a nonexistent command after cancellation and throw.

behavior: Choose form defaults according to nullable field type
trigger: Default generation receives nullable String/ID/LanguageCode/Boolean and numeric/date fields, including lists.
expected: String/ID use empty text, LanguageCode uses supplied/default language, Boolean false, numeric/date scalars null, lists empty arrays.
violation_example: A nullable date receives empty text or a nullable list receives null.

behavior: Keep unknown custom-field object defaults as objects
trigger: Nullable customFields has no typeInfo or uses JSON scalar representation.
expected: Default is an empty object rather than null.
violation_example: Form schema rejects null for an object-valued custom field.

behavior: Convert nullable non-string empty values recursively
trigger: Values contain empty nullable non-strings, empty Strings and required fields in objects and list elements.
expected: Only empty nullable non-strings become null; string and required fields are retained at every nested level.
violation_example: Empty String becomes null or a nested list date stays empty.

behavior: Omit only null nullable fields recursively
trigger: Objects and list elements have null nullable fields, non-null values and required null fields.
expected: Delete nullable null properties and preserve other properties.
violation_example: Delete required or non-null fields, or leave a nullable null nested in a list.

behavior: Leave input values unchanged during conversion and stripping
trigger: Either helper processes nested form values.
expected: Return the transformed copy and retain original nested values.
violation_example: Deleting from a nested original object changes the form state.

behavior: Apply null normalization differently to create and update submissions
trigger: Submit a generated form with no entity versus an existing entity after clearing an optional date.
expected: Both convert empty non-strings; only creation omits nullable nulls, while updating preserves explicit null to clear the value.
violation_example: The hook strips null during update so clearing a value has no effect, or never calls the conversion helper.

behavior: Remove a shipping line whose shipping method no longer exists
trigger: Order includes a shipping line retained by the order-line association filter, but findOne returns undefined for its shippingMethodId.
expected: The stale shipping line is absent after applyPriceAdjustments.
violation_example: The stale line remains in order.shippingLines.

behavior: Continue pricing valid shipping lines after encountering a stale one
trigger: The retained shippingLines array contains a stale line followed by a valid line whose method applies price 500 and tax 20%.
expected: The later valid line is priced: shipping 500, shippingWithTax 600 and corresponding totals.
violation_example: Remove the stale line but return immediately, leaving the valid line unpriced.

behavior: Product pricing uses the active channel tax zone
trigger: One request context prices a variant in channel A, then switches to channel B with a different default tax zone.
expected: ProductPriceApplicator computes B tax using B zone, and switching back still computes A tax using A zone.
violation_example: A shared cache entry causes channel B to reuse the tax zone calculated for A.

behavior: Order calculation uses the active channel tax zone
trigger: An order is calculated under two channels with different tax zones using a context whose channel changes.
expected: OrderCalculator resolves the tax zone for each active channel rather than reusing the other channel cached value.
violation_example: The second channel inherits the first channel tax zone from an unscoped cache entry.

behavior: Address changes invalidate the current channel tax zone
trigger: Shipping or billing address changes after tax zones for multiple channels have been cached.
expected: Both tax-zone cache entries for the active channel are cleared, so subsequent pricing recalculates them without clearing another channel.
violation_example: The active channel retains stale tax-zone entries, or an address edit clears every channel indiscriminately.
